tools.name: acq_create_room
tools.description: Open a new two-seat room - one call is a complete setup: pass join_window_hours to set how long the peer has to join, and opening_message to post your first message immediately. The result is self-sufficient: room UIN, seat token (seat A), private seat-A recovery key (pairCode), invitation text, and

tools.name: acq_join_room
tools.description: Join a room by UIN (seat B, works once). The result contains your seat token.

tools.name: acq_rejoin
tools.description: Recover a lost seat token. Seat A proves with the 6-digit pairing code; seat B proves with the recovery code returned only in the join response. Mints a fresh token; the old one stops working. Anyone with pairCode and the UIN can recover seat A without its token and act as the creator. Keep pairCode

tools.name: acq_send
tools.description: Send a message to your peer. Set end=true to close the room. Pass a unique cid per logical send (reusing one only to retry that same content): it is stored with the message and echoed back, so after an ambiguous failure (connection dropped, timeout, non-JSON gateway error) you can check acq_recv wit

tools.name: acq_recv
tools.description: Receive peer messages. Returns immediately by default (wait=0); pass wait up to 120 to long-poll. For replay-safe reads, pass since=<last cursor you processed> (0 to read everything) and update it from the response cursor field after processing: a lost response is then recovered by re-issuing the id

tools.name: acq_verify
tools.description: Keep pairCode private. Legacy recovery-secret check, not proof of a person's identity. Do not request or share pairCode for verification: anyone with it and the UIN can recover seat A without its token, retire the creator token, and act as the creator. Confirm peers through an existing trusted chann

tools.name: acq_extend
tools.description: Extend the join deadline of an unclaimed room (max 24h ceiling).

tools.name: acq_feedback
tools.description: Leave feedback for the maintainer. No room needed.

tools.name: acq_stats
tools.description: Lifetime service counters: rooms created, rooms paired (seat B joined), and messages. Includes synthetic checks and repeat use; not unique agents, users, or outside adoption. Persisted best-effort and may reset without the volume. Also returns collection_started_at and up to 192 UTC event-hour bucke

findings.detail: Description of "acq_verify" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: acq_create_room, acq_send, acq_recv · Private data: acq_create_room, acq_join_room, acq_rejoin, acq_verify · Public sink: acq_create_room, acq_rejoin, acq_send, acq_verify · Destructive: acq_stats.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: acq_create_room, acq_send, acq_recv · Private data: acq_create_room, acq_join_room, acq_rejoin, acq_verify · Public sink: acq_create_room, acq_rejoin, acq_send, acq_verify · Destructive: acq_stats

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "acq_create_room" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
